title: Curiosity Compounds: Casey Adams on podcasting as a life and business engine
summary: Casey Adams reflects on eight years and 400+ episodes of hosting, and how his podcast became the foundation for his companies, his angel round, and his network. He covers where podcasting is going, how he preps interviews, why curiosity and showing up beat strategy, and the thinking behind his new company Listener.com.

principles.text: Use a podcast as a vehicle for business, not just content: it opens doors to capital, partners and relationships.
principles.quote: during my first uh tech startup we raised round of funding from 37 angel investors and pretty much 90% of the investors were past guests on my podcast

principles.text: Podcasting is still early, and competition is high but there is room to find a unique voice.
principles.quote: there's more competition than ever, but there's still so much room to find your unique voice if you are someone that's looking to step into this world.

principles.text: Prepare for interviews lightly so the process stays exciting and sustainable over years.
principles.quote: what's allowed me to be so like have longevity and have so much excitement about every single interview I still do is because I don't make the preparation for each show like so daunting

principles.text: Attach stories, rules and quotes to lessons so they stick and shape daily behavior.
principles.quote: having rules and laws and stories to reference in your life of why you do things I think is super empowering

principles.text: Cultivate relationships with peers and people around you now, since they become tomorrow's movers and shakers.
principles.quote: the people that are right around you today are the people like the movers and shakers of tomorrow.

principles.text: There is no strategy for spotting rising talent; curiosity about everyone, and saying yes to rooms and opportunities, is the edge.
principles.quote: I don't think there's a strategy to it. I think it's just a a curiosity, right?
